history.dynasty: Golconda Qutb Shahi (builder was a tahsildar under the Sultanate)
history.summary: The Sita Ramachandraswamy Temple at Bhadrachalam, on the northern bank of the Godavari at Bhadragiri hill, is the most famous Rama temple associated with the Khammam region. Legend holds that the devotee Pokala Dhammaka dreamed of the idols in the forest and built a small shrine; the present temple was constructed by Kancherla Gopanna, better known as the saint Bhakta Ramdas, who was the tahsildar (revenue officer) of Palvoncha under the Golconda Qutb Shahi Sultanate. Rama, Sita and Lakshmana are traditionally believed to have spent part of their vanavasa in this Dandakaranya region (Parnasala is ~35 km away), and the temple has the rare distinction of centuries of Muslim patronage — including the legend of the Muslim-born devotee Kabirdas. CORRECTIONS: (1) CSV town 'Khammam' is wrong — the temple is at Bhadrachalam town, ~110-115 km from Khammam city; corrected to Bhadrachalam. (2) District: Bhadrachalam is in Bhadradri Kothagudem district (carved out of the former Khammam district in 2016) — older sources listing 'Khammam district' are now outdated; corrected. State (Telangana) is correct.

name: Sri Seetha Ramachandra Swamy Temple (Bhadrachalam)
town_description: Bhadrachalam is a temple town in Bhadradri Kothagudem district, Telangana, on the northern bank of the Godavari, about 115 km from Khammam and 325 km east of Hyderabad. Named after the Bhadragiri hill, it is associated with the Ramayana's Dandakaranya forest and is one of South India's most important Rama pilgrimage centres.
